summary: 古人珍视龙涎香的香气，却长期将它与琥珀混淆，也难以解释它如何形成。文章追溯它与抹香鲸及难消化的乌贼喙的关系，再说明捕鲸如何影响人们在海上发现它的机会。
logic: 古代用途引出由来之谜
从气味和质地分清龙涎香与琥珀
追溯抹香鲸觅食与消化的关系
说明分泌物如何形成芳香蜡块
联系鲸群数量与海上发现

paragraphs.brief: 在古代世界中，我们现称为安培的蜡灰物质因其药用特性而备受珍视，并被广泛用作一种香料，在添加食物或葡萄酒时，这种香料被认为是一种春药。
sentences: In the ancient world, the waxy grey substance we now refer to as ambergris was highly prized for its medicinal properties, and was widely used as a spice, which was believed to be an aphrodisiac when added to food or wine.
在古代世界中，我们现称为安培的蜡灰物质因其药用特性而备受珍视，并被广泛用作一种香料，在添加食物或葡萄酒时，这种香料被认为是一种春药。

Ambergris itself is pleasantly aromatic, especially when warmed, and it was also highly valued as a fixing agent in the making of perfume, since it enabled a scent to retain its fragrance for much longer than might otherwise have been possible.
Ambergris本身是香味的，特别是暖和的时候，它作为香水制造的固定剂也受到高度的重视，因为它使香味能够保持更长的香味。
Most ambergris was found in the form of lumps floating on the surface of the sea, or washed up on the shores of tropical and temperate oceans.
大部分安贝里以浮在海面或冲到热带和温带海洋海岸的块状物的形式被发现。
At one time, ambergris was worth its weight in gold, but there was much confusion about its origins.
有一次，安贝里斯在黄金中的价值很高，但对于它的起源却有很大的混淆。

paragraphs.brief: Ambergris在阿拉伯人中被称为“阿姆巴尔”，最初在中世纪被称为西方的琥珀。
sentences: Ambergris was known to the Arabs as ‘ambar’ and was originally called amber in the West in the Middle Ages.
Ambergris在阿拉伯人中被称为“阿姆巴尔”，最初在中世纪被称为西方的琥珀。

This eventually led to further confusion in the popular mind between ambergris and true amber, the mineral known to mineralogists as succinite, which is actually fossilised tree resin, and generally yellow in colour.
这最终导致人们在人们的脑海中进一步混淆了安贝里斯和真正的安伯尔，即矿物学家们所知道的杂碎矿，它实际上是化石化的树脂，一般是黄色的。
Both substances were rare and costly, and both were associated with the sea, largely because for Europeans the most common source of amber was the shores of the Baltic.
这两种物质都很少见，而且费用昂贵，两者都与海洋有关，这主要是因为对欧洲人来说，最常用的琥珀来源是波罗的海海岸。

In Chapter 92 of Moby Dick, the American writer Herman Melville pours scorn on those who believed the two substances to be the same: ‘Though the word ambergris is but the French compound for grey amber, yet the two substances are quite distinct.
美国作家赫尔曼·梅尔维尔(Herman Melville)在《Moby Dick》第92章中，对那些认为这两种物质相同的人表示鄙视：“尽管安贝里斯一词只是法国的灰黄复合物，但这两种物质是完全不同的。
For amber, though at times found on the sea-coast, is also dug up in some far-inland soils, whereas ambergris is never found except upon the sea.
对于琥珀，虽然有时在海礁上发现，也在某些遥远的陆地土壤中被挖出，而除了在海中，龙虾是永远找不到的。

Besides, amber is a hard, transparent, brittle, odourless substance, used for mouth-pieces to pipes, for beads and ornaments; but ambergris is soft, waxy, and so highly fragrant that it is largely used in perfumery.’
此外，琥珀是一种硬的、透明的、易碎的、无味的物质，用于管道的口袋、珠子和装饰品；但安贝利柔软、蜡质和香味很强，基本上用于香水。

paragraphs.brief: 但马可波罗想象到鲸鱼吞下了海深的块状物，施韦迪亚沃则表明物料的起源在鲸鱼体内。
sentences: Moby Dick was published in 1851, by which time the mystery of the origins of ambergris had been resolved by the scientific community.
Moby Dick于1851年出版，当时科学界已经解决了安贝里斯起源的谜团。

In 1783, the botanist Joseph Banks, who had accompanied Captain James Cook on his voyages of discovery in the Pacific, presented a paper to the Royal Society of London by the German physician Dr Franz Xavier Schwediawer in which it was conclusively proved that ambergris came from sperm whales.
1783年，陪同詹姆斯·库克船长前往太平洋探险的植物学家约瑟夫·班克斯向伦敦皇家学会提交了德国医生Franz Xavier Schwediawer博士撰写的论文，其中确凿地证明安贝里来自精鲸。

In this, he was confirming an observation made in the 13ᵗʰ century by the great Venetian traveller Marco Polo who, while on the island of Socotra in the Indian Ocean, had witnessed a sperm whale vomiting up ambergris.
他证实了伟大的威尼斯旅行者马科·波罗在13世纪的观察，他在印度洋索科特拉岛上亲眼目睹了一只精子鲸呕吐了安贝里斯。
But whereas Marco Polo imagined that the whale had swallowed the lump in the depths of the sea, Schwediawer showed that the origin of the material was inside the whale itself.
但马可波罗想象到鲸鱼吞下了海深的块状物，施韦迪亚沃则表明物料的起源在鲸鱼体内。

paragraphs.brief: 鲸鱼是最大的鱼或齿鲸
sentences: The sperm whale is the largest of the odontocetes, or toothed whales.
鲸鱼是最大的鱼或齿鲸
Males can grow up to 20 metres in length.
男性可以长到20米长。
Melville described the sperm whale as ‘the king of whales’, and his novel Moby Dick is based on the pursuit of one such creature.
Melville形容精鲸为“鲸王”，他的小说《Moby Dick》是基于对一种这种动物的追求。

Sperm whales are renowned for their ability to dive to great depths, possibly as far as 3 000 metres below the surface, and for remaining underwater for periods of two hours or more in pursuit of their favourite prey, the giant squid.
斑马鲸因其能够潜到极深的海面以下3 000米处和在水下停留两小时或更长时间以追寻其最喜爱的猎物 -- -- 巨型鱿鱼 -- -- 而闻名。

paragraphs.brief: 鲸鱼在消化这种动物的嘴时遇到的问题起源于安贝里斯
sentences: It is from the problems the whales have in digesting the beaks of such creatures that ambergris has its origins.
鲸鱼在消化这种动物的嘴时遇到的问题起源于安贝里斯
The beak is sharp and irritates the whale’s lower intestine, which responds by producing a black, foul-smelling liquid.
嘴尖尖，刺激鲸鱼的下肠，产生一种黑色的、腐烂的液体。

It is not clear to scientists whether this secretion should be considered a normal response by the whale’s digestive system or a pathological one, but from time to time large quantities of the liquid are vomited up by the whale.
科学家们不清楚这种分泌是否应被视为鲸鱼消化系统或病理系统的一种正常反应，但鲸鱼有时会呕吐大量液体。
Once outside the whale’s body and exposed to air, the substance hardens, acquiring the waxy, greyish and pleasantly aromatic characteristics of ambergris.
一旦在鲸鱼身体外暴露在空气中，该物质就会硬化，获得黄蜡、灰色和愉快的芳香特性。
Often the beaks of squid are still found embedded in lumps of ambergris, some of which can weigh several hundred kilograms.
鱿鱼的嘴往往仍被嵌在安贝里状物中，其中一些重达数百公斤。

Melville took some delight in contrasting the origins of ambergris with the high value placed upon it by refined society: ‘Who would think, then, that such fine ladies and gentlemen should regale themselves with an essence found in the inglorious bowels of a sick whale!’
梅尔维尔乐于将安贝里斯的起源与精细社会赋予它的崇高价值作一对比：“谁能想到这些优秀的女士和绅士们应该用一头不光彩的鲸鱼的肠子中的精华来重新塑写自己呢!”

paragraphs.brief: 19世纪和20世纪，商业捕鲸者无情地追寻了斑马鲸。
sentences: Sperm whales were ruthlessly pursued by commercial whalers in the 19ᵗʰ and 20ᵗʰ centuries.
19世纪和20世纪，商业捕鲸者无情地追寻了斑马鲸。
In 1963-64 alone, almost 30 000 individuals were killed, and only the imposition of a ban on the hunting of sperm whales in 1984 saved the species from extinction.
仅在1963-64年，就有近30 000人被杀，只有1984年禁止捕杀精鲸才使该物种免于灭绝。

Ambergris was by far the most valuable product to be extracted during the processing of the whales’ carcasses, and over 90 per cent of the annual worldwide total was acquired in this way, as a by-product of commercial whaling.
Ambergri是迄今为止在加工鲸鱼尸体过程中最有价值的产品，全世界每年90%以上的产品都是以这种方式获得的，作为商业捕鲸的副产品。
However, even before the ban on hunting sperm whales was imposed, the 1972 Marine Mammal Protection Act had prohibited trade in ambergris.
然而，即使在禁止捕杀精鲸之前，1972年的《海洋哺乳动物保护法》就已经禁止了安贝里斯的买卖。

Just as petroleum and plastic products were replacing other natural products of whaling, so ambergris was supplanted in the making of perfume by other materials, some natural and some synthetic in origin.
正如石油和塑料产品正在取代其他天然捕鲸产品一样，安贝里斯也用其他材料代替香水，有些是天然的，有些是合成的。

Nevertheless, it is possible that, as sperm-whale populations recover to their former numbers in the wild, so the sight of lumps of ambergris washed ashore along the tide-line will once again become a familiar one to beach-combers the world over.
然而，随着精液捕食群恢复到原来在野生的数量，因此，看到在潮水线上冲上岸的山脊块将再次成为全世界海滩的熟悉动物。

items.why: 鲸尸加工曾提供全球年度龙涎香总量的九成以上，显然占大多数。

items.en: The value of ambergris has increased recently.
items.zh: 最近安贝里酒的价值有所上升。
